name: Emoji and glyph rendering
plain: Renders emoji and rare Unicode characters and measures or hashes how they look.
meaning: Each OS and version ships a different emoji font and Unicode level, so the rendered glyph set pins the OS, its version and sometimes the vendor skin on Android.

web.api: canvas fillText('emoji'); measureText(); DOM span width

steps: Draw a list of recent emoji to canvas
Compare width or pixels against known OS renderings
Record which glyphs fall back to tofu boxes

data.metric: Pixel or width signature of 20 to 100 Unicode samples

limits.headline: Can draw emoji to tell your system and version apart
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Draw emoji and rare symbols out of sight
Check how they look, since each system uses a different emoji font
Work out your system and often its version
Spot some Android brands from their emoji style
cannot: Know who you are by itself
Get exact results when browsers add noise or use a fixed emoji font

story.what_it_is: A script draws emoji and rare characters and measures how they look, which shows your system and fonts.
story.for_you: You never see it. The page draws a row of emoji out of sight. Apple, Google, Microsoft and Samsung all draw them differently, so the result says a lot about your device.
story.for_makers: Emoji look different on every platform, so this reveals the system and its version very fast. Fraud tools use it to catch emulators, and tracking tools add it to a device ID.

use_cases.example: A bot checker draws a new emoji, sees it as a blank box, and learns the device is running an old system.
A web chat app picks which emoji picture set to show so your messages look the same on every device.
A social site uses one fixed emoji set so a post does not look different in each browser.
A tracker draws emoji with the canvas and hashes the result as part of an anonymous ID.
A browser game with chat checks that your device can show a new emoji, or it swaps in an image.
A visitor counting tool uses the emoji look to split visitors on iOS from Android.
A kids learning site checks that emoji used in lessons display properly, or uses pictures instead.

technical_bounds: Reveals OS and font stack but not per-device identity
Fallback fonts may be user-installed, adding entropy

value.legit_uses: Detect missing emoji support and show fallbacks
value.abuse: Narrow OS version, cloak-detect spoofed user agents

history.change: Emoji sets used in FingerprintJS and CreepJS to detect OS version
